coverage:
All 59 reviewed input categories survive synthesis. No two categories share an id, and no two share a seed_doc_id set such that one is a strict superset of the other, so no rows were dropped in dedup; the conceptual overlaps the slices flagged are now made explicit in notes (see "DEDUPE NOTE" entries). Coverage by business_structure:

- none (employee individual): wre_* D1-D5 family (car, travel, clothing/laundry, protective/PPE, self-education, WFH fixed + actual, phone/internet, tools, union/professional fees, income-protection D15, seminars/subscriptions, occupation-specific), plus the no-trigger personal items wre_gifts_donations, wre_managing_tax_affairs, and all structures=[all] super/insurance/offset categories. Investors who are not in business are also reachable via has_investment_property / has_shares_or_managed_funds / has_crypto since those triggers list 'none' among structures.
- sole_trader: gets BOTH the personal WRE set (a sole trader who is also an employee) AND the dedicated st_* business set (motor vehicle, home-based business, operating expenses, trading stock/COGS, depreciating assets + IAWO, small-business pool, professional fees, business insurance, phone/internet, repairs/maintenance, bad debts, personal super) gated on has_abn. Investor and super categories also apply.
- partnership: covered at the partner's personal level by rental_* (has_investment_property), shares/crypto (has_*), all super/insurance/offset categories (structures=[all]), wre_gifts_donations and wre_managing_tax_affairs; and at the entity level by ent_general_operating_8_1, ent_salaries_wages_super, ent_depreciating_assets, ent_instant_asset_write_off_sb_pool, ent_motor_vehicle_entity_owned, ent_premises_occupancy, ent_professional_compliance_fees, ent_business_insurance, ent_interest_business_borrowings, ent_trading_stock (gated has_abn). Note partnership net income/loss flows to partners — see gaps.
- company: ent_* entity set (incl. company-only ent_directors_fees, ent_prior_year_tax_losses, ent_rd_tax_incentive) plus the structures=[all] personal super/insurance/offset/gift/tax-affairs categories that a director-shareholder claims on their own return.
- trust: same ent_* set as company minus ent_directors_fees and ent_rd_tax_incentive (correctly excluded); ent_prior_year_tax_losses applies (Sch 2F trust loss rules); plus structures=[all] personal categories for beneficiaries.

Investors: has_investment_property surfaces 8 rental categories (interest, Div43 capital works, Div40 decline-in-value, repairs-vs-improvements, holding/admin fees, borrowing costs, the s 26-31 travel DISALLOWANCE flag, the s 26-102 vacant-land LIMITATION flag). has_shares_or_managed_funds surfaces 2 (D7 borrowing interest, D8 management/platform fees). has_crypto surfaces 2 (CGT-on-disposal + 50% discount, trading-stock-vs-investment classification).

SMSF members: smsf_member_personal_super_deduction is gated on super_fund_type='smsf' and explicitly disambiguates the member's PERSONAL-return deduction from the SMSF entity's OWN deductions (which are out of scope for this personal-focused taxonomy — flagged in gaps).

Thresholds used (all allow-listed): cgt_discount_individual, instant_asset_write_off, super_concessional_cap. No disallowed threshold names appear.
edge_cases: Sole trader who is ALSO an employee: must surface BOTH the wre_* personal D1-D5 set (their employment use) AND the st_* business set (their ABN business use). wre_car (employment car use, D1, cents-per-km/logbook) and st_business_motor_vehicle (business car use) are distinct rows that can BOTH fire; the runtime must not let the same kilometres be claimed twice across the two.

Sole trader with NO occupation but an ABN: occupation-gated wre_* categories will NOT fire (trigger occupation:truthy fails) while has_abn-gated st_* categories will. Conversely an employee with an occupation but no ABN gets wre_* but no st_*. Confirm the facts capture both occupation and has_abn independently.

Company director who is also a personal investor: ent_directors_fees and entity categories fire on the company return (has_abn), while their personal rental/shares/crypto/super categories fire on their individual return — two different return_context outputs from one taxpayer's combined facts. The tool must clearly label which return each category belongs to.

Resident vs non_resident vs working_holiday_maker vs temporary_resident: the current triggers DO NOT gate on residency_status, so deductions surface identically for all. In reality foreign/working-holiday-maker taxpayers have restricted offsets (no tax-free threshold for WHM income, no CGT 50% discount accrued while non-resident on assets acquired/held as a foreign resident post-8 May 2012), and non-residents generally cannot access the main-residence-related concessions. crypto_cgt_on_disposal's cgt_discount_individual and st_home_based_business CGT framing need a residency caveat at runtime.

SMSF member nuance: smsf_member_personal_super_deduction is the MEMBER's personal-return claim; the SMSF fund's own deductions (insurance premiums s 295-465, fund admin/audit, actuarial costs) are entity-level on the SMSF annual return and are intentionally absent — the tool must not imply the member can claim the fund's expenses.

Double-counting WFH: wre_wfh_fixed_rate bundles phone+internet+energy+stationery; wre_phone_internet and parts of wre_wfh_actual cover the same costs. All three can surface (recall-first) but the consider_prompts warn against claiming the same cost twice — runtime should enforce mutual exclusivity of fixed-rate vs actual for the same hours.

Income-protection appears in THREE places (wre_income_protection_insurance occupation-gated, income_protection_insurance_premiums all-structures, and as a line in st_business_insurance). Dedup at merge so a single IP premium is presented once.

Personal super deduction appears in personal_super_concessional_deduction (all structures), st_personal_super_contribution (sole_trader subset), and smsf_member_personal_super_deduction (SMSF subset) — all the same s 290-150 deduction. Merge logic must collapse to one claim while preserving the structure-specific consider_prompt.

Rental property held in a company or trust name: the rental_* categories are gated to structures [sole_trader, partnership, none] and return_context=personal, matching individual/partnership ownership. A rental held by a company/trust would instead surface entity categories — but has_investment_property is a personal fact, so a director whose COMPANY owns the rental could mis-trigger personal rental categories. Runtime should reconcile property ownership with the entity.

Spouse offset is an OFFSET not a deduction (spouse_super_contribution_offset) — must not be summed into a 'total deductions' figure. Same caution for the FHSS released amount (assessable income, not a deduction) and the personal_super_notice_of_intent gate (a precondition, zero dollars itself).

Vacant-land (s 26-102) and rental-travel (s 26-31) are DISALLOWANCE/limitation flags, not positive deductions. The tool must render them as warnings so the recall-first surfacing does not read as 'you can claim this'.

prior_fy_lodged false: ent_prior_year_tax_losses is gated on prior_fy_lodged:truthy — a first-year entity with current-year losses cannot carry FORWARD yet (there is no prior loss), but it CAN carry the current loss forward to next year; the category copy is about USING a brought-forward loss, which is correct to suppress in year 1.
open_questions: Residency gating: should we add residency_status triggers (or runtime caveats) to suppress/qualify categories for non_resident / working_holiday_maker / temporary_resident taxpayers (no tax-free threshold for WHM, restricted CGT discount, no main-residence concessions)? Currently NO category gates on residency. Product decision: hard-gate vs soft-warn.

Merge vs surface for the three identical s 290-150 super-deduction rows (personal_super_concessional_deduction, st_personal_super_contribution, smsf_member_personal_super_deduction): should the orchestrator collapse them to one card with a structure-specific note, or present all three? The recall-first principle argues surface; the no-double-counting principle argues merge. Same question for the two income-protection rows.

Should offsets (spouse super offset) and assessable-income items (crypto CGT, FHSS released amount) live in a deduction_discovery tool at all, or be split into a separate 'tax position' surface? They are included here for recall but are not deductions, which risks confusing a 'total deductions' UI.

Entity-vs-individual rental ownership reconciliation: has_investment_property is a single boolean with no owner field. Do we need a follow-up fact (property held personally vs in entity) to avoid surfacing personal rental_* categories when the property is company/trust-owned?

Scope of business-entity coverage: the taxonomy is deliberately personal-return-centric. Should we expand the entity slice to a full company/trust/partnership/SMSF deduction set (FBT deductibility, business start-up s 40-880, prepaid expenses, R&D for the trust-with-corporate-beneficiary case, SMSF fund-level deductions), or keep deduction_discovery focused on the individual taxpayer and defer entity completeness to a separate tool?

Activity-text handling: ent_rd_tax_incentive and the occupation/industry catch-all rely on free-text activity input because no facts field captures R&D or specific industry deductions. What is the runtime contract for using activity text to confirm/boost a category before surfacing it prominently?

FY-rolling thresholds: instant_asset_write_off, super_concessional_cap, cgt_discount_individual and the cents-per-km rate / car depreciation limit change each FY. Confirm the runtime always resolves these via get_threshold rather than the literals in examples/substantiation, and that current_fy is honoured (e.g. the GIC/SIC deductibility cutoff at 1 July 2025 in wre_managing_tax_affairs).

test_scenarios.name: employee_nurse_wfh
test_scenarios.facts: business_structure=none, occupation='registered nurse', no abn, works from home some days, has_spouse=false
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface wre_clothing_laundry, wre_protective_ppe, wre_self_education, wre_wfh_fixed_rate, wre_wfh_actual, wre_phone_internet, wre_tools_equipment, wre_union_professional_fees, wre_occupation_specific (resolves to nurses/midwives guide), wre_gifts_donations, wre_managing_tax_affairs, personal_super_concessional_deduction. SHOULD NOT surface any st_* (no abn), any ent_* (structure=none), rental_*/shares_*/crypto_* (no investor facts), spouse_super_contribution_offset (no spouse).

test_scenarios.name: sole_trader_tradie_also_employed
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface BOTH wre_* (occupation truthy: car, travel, protective/PPE, tools, etc.) AND st_* business set (st_business_motor_vehicle, st_operating_expenses, st_depreciating_assets_iawo, st_repairs_maintenance, st_phone_internet, st_business_insurance, st_professional_fees, st_personal_super_contribution, st_home_based_business). SHOULD NOT surface ent_* (business_entity rows are for company/trust/partnership) or ent_directors_fees.

test_scenarios.name: company_director_with_rental_and_crypto
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface entity rows on the COMPANY return: ent_general_operating_8_1, ent_salaries_wages_super, ent_directors_fees, ent_depreciating_assets, ent_instant_asset_write_off_sb_pool, ent_motor_vehicle_entity_owned, ent_premises_occupancy, ent_professional_compliance_fees, ent_business_insurance, ent_interest_business_borrowings, ent_trading_stock, ent_prior_year_tax_losses, ent_rd_tax_incentive. SHOULD surface on the director's PERSONAL return: rental_* (8 rows incl. disallowance flags), crypto_cgt_on_disposal, crypto_trading_stock_vs_investment, personal_super_concessional_deduction, income_protection_insurance_premiums. SHOULD NOT surface wre_* (company has no work-related-expense personal concept tied to occupation here) unless occupation is set; SHOULD NOT surface st_* (not a sole trader).

test_scenarios.name: trust_no_directors_no_rd
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface ent_general_operating_8_1, ent_salaries_wages_super, ent_depreciating_assets, ent_instant_asset_write_off_sb_pool, ent_motor_vehicle_entity_owned, ent_premises_occupancy, ent_professional_compliance_fees, ent_business_insurance, ent_interest_business_borrowings, ent_trading_stock, ent_prior_year_tax_losses. SHOULD NOT surface ent_directors_fees (company-only) or ent_rd_tax_incentive (company-only).

test_scenarios.name: smsf_member_individual
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface smsf_member_personal_super_deduction (gated super_fund_type=smsf), personal_super_concessional_deduction, personal_super_notice_of_intent, personal_super_carry_forward_concessional, plus occupation-gated wre_* set. SHOULD NOT surface SMSF FUND-level deductions (out of scope) and SHOULD NOT surface st_*/ent_* (no abn, structure=none).

test_scenarios.name: share_investor_with_spouse_no_occupation
test_scenarios.facts: business_structure=none, has_shares_or_managed_funds=true, has_spouse=true, no occupation, no abn
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface shares_borrowing_interest (D7), shares_management_advice_and_platform_fees (D8), spouse_super_contribution_offset (has_spouse), personal_super_concessional_deduction, income_protection_insurance_premiums, wre_gifts_donations, wre_managing_tax_affairs. SHOULD NOT surface any occupation-gated wre_* (no occupation), rental_* (no property), crypto_* (no crypto), st_*/ent_*.

test_scenarios.name: partnership_partner_with_property
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface entity rows: ent_general_operating_8_1, ent_salaries_wages_super, ent_depreciating_assets, ent_instant_asset_write_off_sb_pool, ent_motor_vehicle_entity_owned, ent_premises_occupancy, ent_professional_compliance_fees, ent_business_insurance, ent_interest_business_borrowings, ent_trading_stock. SHOULD surface personal rental_* (structures include partnership). SHOULD NOT surface ent_prior_year_tax_losses (excludes partnership), ent_directors_fees, ent_rd_tax_incentive, or st_* (sole-trader-only).

test_scenarios.name: working_holiday_maker_employee
test_scenarios.facts: business_structure=none, residency_status=working_holiday_maker, occupation='fruit picker', no abn
test_scenarios.expect: Under current triggers SHOULD surface the occupation-gated wre_* set identically to a resident (NO residency gate exists). This scenario documents the known gap: the tool should attach a residency caveat (WHM income taxed from first dollar, restricted offsets) — see open_questions. Asserts that residency is NOT currently a gate.

test_scenarios.name: first_year_sole_trader_loss
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface st_* business set and occupation-gated wre_* set. SHOULD NOT surface ent_prior_year_tax_losses (gated has_abn AND prior_fy_lodged truthy; prior_fy_lodged is false AND it is an entity-only category anyway for company/trust).

test_scenarios.name: crypto_trader_classification
test_scenarios.facts: business_structure=none, has_crypto=true, activity_text='I trade crypto full-time, hundreds of trades a month'
test_scenarios.expect: SHOULD surface crypto_cgt_on_disposal AND crypto_trading_stock_vs_investment so the trader-vs-investor distinction is flagged (recall-first). Runtime should use activity_text to lean toward the trading-stock branch but still present both. SHOULD NOT auto-apply the 50% CGT discount without resolving classification.

gaps: FBT-as-a-deduction to the employer entity: a real category (employer's FBT liability is deductible under s 8-1; TR 95/24 'Income tax: deductibility of fringe benefits tax' exists in corpus as ato-law:TXR/TR9524/NAT/ATO/00001) is NOT modelled. fbt_payer is a facts field with no corresponding category. Worth adding as an entity-level row.

Business start-up / blackhole expenditure (s 40-880, verified in corpus as legis:c2004a05138/40-880 titled 'Business related costs'; ATO page 'Certain start-up expenses immediately deductible' exists): no category captures deductible business establishment/professional-advice costs for a new entity or sole trader. Only referenced in passing in st_professional_fees notes.

Prepaid expenses regime: corpus has dedicated 'Deductions for prepaid expenses' pages, but no category models the prepayment rules (immediate deduction for small business / 12-month rule vs apportionment). Relevant to both st_* and ent_* slices; only mentioned in ent_business_insurance notes.

GST input-tax-credit / income-tax-deduction interaction: corpus has 'Effect of GST credits on income tax deductions'. For GST-registered taxpayers the deductible amount is the GST-exclusive cost — no category surfaces this netting rule despite gst_registered being a facts field.

SMSF fund-level deductions (the fund's OWN return): insurance premiums (s 295-465), administration, audit, actuarial and investment-management costs deductible to the SMSF. Deliberately scoped out of this personal-return taxonomy, but a genuine gap if deduction_discovery is later extended to entity returns. Flagged in smsf_member_personal_super_deduction notes.

Partnership/trust distribution mechanics: partnership net losses flow to partners who claim their share on their OWN returns; no category models the partner-level claim of a partnership loss (ent_prior_year_tax_losses explicitly excludes partnerships). myTax 'Partnerships' and 'partnership or trust distributions' pages exist in corpus but no category targets the partner's personal-return treatment.

Personal-services-income (PSI) deduction restrictions: no category warns that PSI rules can deny certain sole-trader/entity deductions (rent, super for associates, car for non-principal). A recall-first deduction tool risks over-surfacing for PSI-affected taxpayers; no PSI fact or category exists.

Low-income super tax offset (LISTO) and government super co-contribution: mentioned only as consider_prompt nudges, not modelled as categories (they are government-paid amounts, not deductions/offsets the taxpayer claims) — intentional, noted here for completeness.

Donations carried-forward / spreading election over 5 years for gifts of property and conservation covenants (Div 30 spreading): wre_gifts_donations covers the basic DGR gift but not the spreading election — minor sub-feature gap, corpus has Div 30 sections.

blocker_issues.detail: The original example and consider_prompt listed 'ATO general interest charge (GIC) and shortfall interest charge' as claimable. This is WRONG for the current FY. The live corpus page (cost-of-managing-tax-affairs, last updated 26 June 2025) states an ATO interest charge is deductible only 'if it was incurred prior to 1 July 2025'. GIC/SIC deductibility was repealed for charges incurred on or after 1 July 2025. Since current_fy is 2025-26 (today 2026-06-03), surfacing GIC/SIC as claimable would mislead. FIXED: removed GIC/SIC from examples, replaced with valuation/litigation items, and added explicit dating warnings to substantiation, consider_prompt and notes. Also updated 'AAT' to 'Administrative Review Tribunal (ART)' per the live page.
